LESSON: SOIL

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Natural environment
Topic 2.2: Soil
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Soil, part of Natural environment in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we care for soil? 2. How can you protect our soil?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to characteristics of soil,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Soil in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify characteristics of different types of soil,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Soil in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. carry out basic activities of caring for soil in the environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Soil in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. embrace activities of caring for soil. ● In groups, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign words related to characteristics of soil.( loam, clay, sand, texture, mulching) ● Learners are guided in groups to move around the school environment and collect and sign different soil samples. ● The learners are guided to use the sense of touch to interact with various samples of soil (sand, loam and clay soils) to feel their texture. ● Learners are guided in small groups to find out the characteristics of the different soil types and share in class. ● Learners are guided in groups to mount and label different soil samples on a chart and display the chart in class. ● Learners are guided in groups to discuss how to care for soil in the environment (manuring, mulching, planting trees,) and share with peers. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Soil together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
